taxonomy.subtopic: Portal-systemic collateral formation at the distal esophagus

questions.stem_html: A 58-year-old man with alcohol-associated cirrhosis is brought to the emergency department after vomiting a large amount of blood. Endoscopy shows tortuous submucosal veins in the distal esophagus. The accompanying venous map highlights the collateral pathway responsible for these vessels. Which pair of veins forms this portal-systemic connection?

options.text_html: Left gastric vein and esophageal veins that drain into the azygos system
Superior rectal vein and middle rectal veins that drain into the internal iliac system
Paraumbilical veins and superficial epigastric veins of the abdominal wall
Splenic vein and left renal vein through short gastric collaterals
Superior mesenteric vein and inferior vena cava through retroperitoneal veins

questions.explanation_html: At the distal esophagus, the portal left gastric vein communicates with esophageal submucosal veins that drain through the azygos system into the superior vena cava. Portal hypertension drives blood through these fragile collateral channels, producing esophageal varices. The other listed pathways describe different potential portosystemic collateral sites or are anatomically mismatched to distal esophageal varices.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: This is the anorectal portosystemic connection and is associated with rectal varices, not distal esophageal varices.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: This is the periumbilical collateral pathway that can produce caput medusae.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: A splenorenal pathway is more closely associated with gastric or spontaneous splenorenal collaterals than the classic distal esophageal connection.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Retroperitoneal collateral vessels can enlarge in portal hypertension but do not form the characteristic distal esophageal varices.

questions.educational_objective: Esophageal varices arise where the portal left gastric vein communicates with systemic esophageal veins draining to the azygos system.

media.alt_text: Original portal-systemic venous map emphasizing flow from the left gastric vein through distal esophageal collaterals into the azygos system.
